approach: Add `revert_for: Vec<u32>` to CheckRun (athena-data): the criterion numbers whose planned 'fails without the fix' run this record is; empty for every ordinary check (serde default, skipped when empty). Athena builds the record from each finished demonstration run with a pure `revert_record(group, run)` in verify.rs. The name comes from one shared helper `demonstration_name(group)`, which checks.rs (the CheckSpec name), demonstration_entry and revert_record all call, so the shown and recorded names cannot drift. The record keeps the plan's command, exit code, tests_ran and output tail, and has passed = true, meaning 'not a pass/fail check'. This departs from the reading's 'passed means failed as expected'; the field doc, changelog and design doc say so. In judge(), the existing job-wide filter line is untouched. A `continue` at the top of its loop body skips any record with a non-empty revert_for, so an exit-0 revert record (the demonstration still passed without the fix) can never reach the job-wide `ran`. Inside the same candidate_tree == checks_tree gate, revert records that have an exit code go into a separate list. A cited piece for criterion n counts as seen when it is in `ran`, or when a revert record whose revert_for contains n has that command or that record name. run/checks.rs returns each run's view and record together. verification_stage appends the records to check_runs after the verifier's input view is built, so the brief still shows each run once. A run that finished with any exit code counts for its own criteria, because the record shows the run happened and the verifier judges the result. An exit-0 run is shown to the verifier as 'passed without the fix'. A run with no exit code counts for nothing. Carried check lines render a revert record as 'name: revert run (exit code N)'. A small close.rs helper keeps revert records out of the pull-request body's 'N checks passed'.

decisions.choice: Mark the record with `revert_for: Vec<u32>` (criteria it demonstrates) instead of `revert: bool`.
decisions.reason: The 'fails without part only' scope must be enforced by code, and the data exists: judge() walks criteria by index (verify.rs ~470) and DemonstrationGroup.criteria (verify.rs 706-713) holds the numbers. One field is both marker (non-empty) and scope, so they cannot disagree. An empty value means an ordinary check, as `reused` false does.

decisions.choice: Answer finding 2: keep the job-wide filter line byte for byte, and add `if !check.revert_for.is_empty() { continue; }` as the first statement of the loop body at verify.rs 375-381. decisions.reason: A revert record has passed = true, and a run that still passes without the fix exits 0, so it matches the filter at verify.rs 378 and its command would join the job-wide `ran` for every behavior criterion, and it comes from the reverted copy, not the candidate tree. The `continue` stops that without editing the searched text, so the admission test ci_reuse_replay_the_seen_commands_filter_turns_up_in_a_search_and_must_be_named (admission.rs 1078-1143) still finds `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()`. A chained `.filter` before line 378 was rejected only because the `continue` is smaller and leaves the iterator chain, which rustfmt lays out, exactly as it is.

decisions.choice: An exit-0 revert run (demonstration passed without the fix) counts as seen running for its own criteria only; a run with no exit code counts for nothing. The docs say this.
decisions.reason: The seen-running rule asks whether the cited command ran, and the record proves it did. Whether the criterion is met stays the verifier's judgment, and the verifier is shown 'passed without the fix' (run/tests.rs 3164-3186 case). Excluding exit 0 would make the rule depend on the outcome of the run, not on whether it ran. A test pins that an exit-0 record for [3] stays unseen for criterion 2.

rejected.why: It makes 'seen running' depend on the run's result and hides a demonstration that wrongly passes from the 'seen' set without helping the verifier.

decisions.choice: The revert record always has passed = true; its exit code stays as run. Carried lines render it 'name: revert run (exit code N)'.
decisions.reason: Readers treat !passed as a failed check: judge() blocking_checks (verify.rs 384), reading.rs failed-check carry text (~1933), introspect.rs failure_details (939-949), is_pre_existing. rejected.why: A revert run that wrongly passes would block the verdict, breaking 64cb889's 'fails nothing' rule.
